title: Declared routes, canonical URLs, breadcrumbs, and not-found surfaces
iWant: every screen to have a stable, canonical URL that loads correctly on arrival
soThat: I can bookmark, share, and return to anything I can see

acceptanceCriteria.description: The project maintains a declared route inventory naming every route; no navigable surface exists outside it.
acceptanceCriteria.when: the route inventory is compared against reachable navigation targets
acceptanceCriteria.then: every reachable target appears in the inventory and every inventory entry is reachable

acceptanceCriteria.description: Each resource class uses one canonical URL shape; the same resource is never reachable under two shapes without a redirect to the canonical one.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a resource with a canonical URL
acceptanceCriteria.when: a non-canonical variant of that URL is visited
acceptanceCriteria.then: the application redirects or rewrites to the canonical shape

acceptanceCriteria.description: Breadcrumbs render on every route nested more than two levels deep, reflecting the canonical hierarchy, with each ancestor navigable.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a route at nesting depth three or more
acceptanceCriteria.then: a breadcrumb trail shows the ancestry and each crumb navigates to its level

acceptanceCriteria.description: Visiting an unknown path renders the designed 404 surface inside the shell with navigation intact and a way back to a known route.
acceptanceCriteria.when: a path outside the route inventory is visited
acceptanceCriteria.then: the 404 surface renders with shell navigation present, not a blank page or silent redirect

acceptanceCriteria.description: Visiting a resource that previously existed and was removed renders the designed 410 surface distinguishing "gone" from "never existed".
acceptanceCriteria.given: a resource known to be deleted
acceptanceCriteria.then: the 410 surface renders naming the resource as removed

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every route in the inventory cold-loads from a direct URL entry, not only via in-app navigation.
acceptanceCriteria.when: the URL is opened in a fresh browser session
acceptanceCriteria.then: the route renders its arrival state without client-side navigation first
